images.title: Cut the corners: two equal squares
images.purpose: Shows that cutting the four corners of a 4 cm square from midpoint to midpoint leaves a square of 8 square cm, and the four corners make another square of 8 square cm.
images.composition: Plain white background with generous empty margins; the main object is large and centred and fills about 60 percent of the frame; nothing else is drawn. Before and after in one row: the cut square on the left, a thick grey arrow, the four corners put together on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: a square of side 4 units with a thin dark outline. The midpoints of its 4 sides are joined in order by 4 thin dark lines, making a tilted square standing on a corner, filled teal #0072B2. The 4 corner pieces are right triangles with two 2 unit sides, filled amber #E69F00. Below the bottom side: '4 cm'. Inside the teal square: '8 sq cm'. Centre: a thick grey arrow pointing right. Right: the same 4 amber right triangles turned so their 4 right angle corners meet at one centre point, forming a square of exactly the same size as the teal one, also standing on a corner, with thin dark lines between the triangles. Below it: '8 sq cm'. So '8 sq cm' appears twice and '4 cm' once. Nothing else.

images.takeaway: The square left over and the square made from the corners are equal, each half of 16 sq cm.
images.description: Shows that cutting the four corners of a 4 cm square from midpoint to midpoint leaves a square of 8 square cm, and the four corners make another square of 8 square cm.
images.context: Concept T5.C1; one image that shows only the main idea.
images.teaching_notes: 16 square cm in all; each corner 2 × 2 ÷ 2 = 2, four corners 8; left over 16 − 8 = 8.

image_decisions.why: The concept asks the child to see a cut and a rearrangement; drawing it once confirms what was imagined.
